chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does there happen something today that was not in the knowledge of Allah yesterday? He said: No. May the one who says this be abased by Allah! I said: Consider - whatever has happened and whatever will happen up to the Day of Judgment is it not in the knowledge of Allah? He said: Yes. Before He created the creation.
ai.seo_question: What does Shia theology say about whether Allah's knowledge changes over time?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the doctrine of divine omniscience by affirming that all events, from the past to the Day of Judgment, were already known to Allah prior to creation. This directly refutes the notion of 'new knowledge' (jadid) being acquired by God, a key distinction in Shia theology when reconciling divine foreknowledge with the concept of Bada'. The Imam's emphatic response underscores the immutability of God's eternal knowledge, distinguishing it from human temporal experience.
